sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the claimants questioning the quantum determined by the Tribunal in MVC.No.33/2018.
Respondent No.2/Insurance Company admits its liability.
Therefore, the appeal is purely on quantum.
2. The claimants who are the wife, children and mother of deceased filed the claim petition for having lost one Yankoba in a road traffic accident dated 9.1.2018.

The Tribunal in absence of income proof, assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- and without extending the benefit of future prospects awarded a sum of Rs.13,82,400/- under the head of loss of dependency.
In all, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.14,66,210/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

3. This Court on re-appreciation of the material on record is of the view that the Tribunal erred in notionally assessing the income at Rs.9,000/- ignoring the fact that NC: 2024:KHC-K:9486 the accident is of the year 2018.
In the absence of income proof, this Court is inclined to place reliance on the income chart prepared by the Legal Services Authority.
The accident is of the year 2018.
Therefore, the income is notionally assessed at Rs.11,750/-.
By adding 40% towards future prospects, income is assessed at Rs.16,450/-.
After deducting 1/4th, the income works out to Rs.12,338/-.
By applying the multiplier of 16, compensation payable under the head of loss of dependency works out to Rs.23,68,800/-.
4. There are five dependants.
Under the conventional heads, a sum of Rs.2,30,000/- is awarded.
The accident is of the year 2018.

Therefore, 10% escalation on Rs.2,30,000/- which works out to Rs.23,000/- is awarded by following the principles laid down in the case of National Insurance Co.
Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors1.

sentences.text:
Rs. 13,810/- awarded by the 2017 ACJ 2700 SC NC:
2024:KHC-K:9486 Tribunal towards medical expenses is retained.
Thus, total compensation re-determined by this Court works out to Rs.26,35,610/- as against Rs.14,66,210/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The appellants are held entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.11,69,410/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

5. Accordingly, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part;

(ii) The judgment and award dated 26.6.2019 passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.33/2018 is hereby modified;
(iii) The appellants are held entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs. 11,69,410/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization excluding the delay period.
